ing: steaks, such as grouper or snapper
st: Chop the parsley, [[4 clove]] garlic and 1 onion into a rough paste. Stuff it into slits cut in the fish.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large pot. Fry the fish 3 minutes per side and set aside.
In the same oil, cook the second onion, sliced, for 5 minutes. Stir in [[4 tbsp]] tomato paste for 3 minutes.
Add [[6 cup]] water, [[2 tsp]] salt and the chili. Boil, then add the cassava and carrots and cook 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage, eggplant and garlic and cook 15 minutes until tender.
Return the fish, cover, and simmer 8 minutes until it flakes.
Lift out the fish and vegetables. Add the rice to the broth, adding water if needed so it is covered by 1 inch.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until the rice is red and tender.
Serve the rice on a platter topped with fish and vegetables.
Mix the onions, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, [[1 tsp]] pepper and [[2 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add the chicken, rub it well, and marinate in the fridge for 3 hours or overnight.
Lift the chicken out, keeping the onions. Grill or broil it 6 minutes per side until browned.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a heavy pot. Cook the marinade onions and bay leaves 15 minutes on medium heat.
Add the chili, [[1 cup]] broth and chicken. Cover and simmer 35 minutes.
Check the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C), and taste for salt and lemon.
Cook the rice with [[3.5 cup]] water. Serve the chicken and onion sauce over it.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches, about 8 minutes. Remove it.
Cook the onions 5 minutes, then garlic 1 minute. Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Whisk [[0.75 cup]] peanut butter with [[1 cup]] hot water until smooth.
Return the beef, add the peanut mix, [[3 cup]] more water, chili and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Cover and simmer on low for 60 minutes, stirring often.
Add the carrots and sweet potatoes and cook 25 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick with oil on top.
Cook the rice with [[3.5 cup]] water and serve the stew over it.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] palm oil in a pot and cook the onion and garlic 5 minutes.
Add [[3 cup]] water, the whole chili and [[1 tsp]] salt, and bring to a boil.
Add the okra and simmer 12 minutes until the stew thickens.
Add the fish and simmer 6 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook 3 minutes until pink.
Taste and add salt. Remove the chili if too hot.
Serve with rice cooked from [[1.5 cup]] rice and [[2.5 cup]] water.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large pot. Brown the lamb 8 minutes, then add the onions for 5 minutes.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[6 cup]] water. Simmer, covered, for 60 minutes.
Add carrots, turnips and cabbage and cook 25 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and [[2 tsp]] salt for the last 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, sprinkle the couscous with [[1 cup]] water and rub with your fingers. Steam in a steamer set over the pot for 20 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with [[2 tbsp]] butter and a fork.
Check the lamb reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Serve the couscous topped with meat, vegetables and sauce.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot and cook the onions 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper for 1 minute.
Pour in [[4 cup]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and the chili. Simmer 15 minutes.
Slide in the fish and cook gently for 8 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice off the heat.
Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Serve with rice cooked from [[1.5 cup]] rice and [[2.5 cup]] water.

ing: boneless leg or chops, cut in pieces
st: Rub the lamb with [[2 tbsp]] oil, garlic, [[1 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt. Marinate 30 minutes.
Heat a grill or heavy skillet very hot.
Cook the lamb 5 minutes per side until browned, to at least 145°F (63°C).
Rest it for 5 minutes, then chop into bite-sized pieces.
Cook the onions in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 8 minutes. Add [[3 tbsp]] mustard, the chili and [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice and cook 2 minutes.
Pile the grilled meat onto a platter and top with the hot onions.
Serve with fresh bread for scooping up the onions.

ing: cooked and flaked, or canned tuna
st: Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[0.75 cup]] warm water into a firm dough. Knead 5 minutes and rest 20 minutes.
Cook the onion in [[1 tbsp]] oil 5 minutes, then add the garlic, chili and tomatoes for 5 minutes.
Stir in the fish and parsley and cook 3 minutes. Season with salt and cool.
Roll the dough thin and cut 4-inch circles.
Put a spoon of filling on each, fold into half-moons and press the edges with a fork.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain.
Serve the pastels hot, with extra chili sauce if you like.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[0.75 cup]] warm water. Knead 5 minutes and rest 20 minutes.
Brown the beef in a skillet for 8 minutes until cooked through to 160°F (71°C). Drain extra fat.
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, chili and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and cook 6 minutes. Season with salt and cool.
Roll the dough thin and cut 4-inch circles.
Fill each with a spoonful of meat, fold over and seal with a fork.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
Boil the peas in [[4 cup]] water for 60 minutes until very tender.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a pan. Cook the onion 6 minutes, then garlic 1 minute.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and fry 3 minutes.
Add the onion mix and chili to the beans with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Simmer 20 minutes, mashing some beans, until thick.
Toast the baguette halves.
Spread [[1 tbsp]] mustard inside the bread and fill with the bean stew.
Serve the sandwiches hot while the bread is crisp.
Moisten the couscous with [[0.5 cup]] water and rub with your fingers to break up clumps.
Steam over simmering water for 15 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, add [[1 tbsp]] butter, and cool completely.
Soak the raisins in [[0.5 cup]] warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Stir the yogurt, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] vanilla, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and cream together.
Gently fold the cooled couscous and the raisins into the yogurt mixture.
Chill in the fridge for 1 hour before serving.
Serve cold in small bowls.
Rinse the hibiscus flowers well under cold water.
Bring [[8 cup]] water to a boil and add the hibiscus.
Boil 10 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Steep for 20 minutes covered.
Strain the liquid into a pitcher.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar until it dissolves, then [[1 tsp]] vanilla and the mint.
Chill for 2 hours and serve over ice.
Whisk [[0.5 cup]] baobab powder with [[1 cup]] of the cold water in a bowl until you have a smooth paste with no dry lumps.
Add the remaining [[2 cup]] cold water and whisk again until the drink is cloudy and pale cream.
Pour it through a fine strainer into a pitcher, pressing out the liquid and throwing away the fibers and seeds.
Stir in [[0.33 cup]] sugar, [[0.5 cup]] evaporated milk and [[1 tsp]] vanilla until the sugar dissolves.
Taste. It should be sweet with a clear citrus tang, so add more sugar if it is too sour.
Chill for 1 hour, stir well, and serve over ice.
nt: No cook: whisk, strain and chill
Best swap: coconut milk in place of the evaporated milk for a dairy-free version, 1 to 1.

st: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, pepper and a pinch of salt. Marinate the fish in half of it for 30 minutes.
Toss the onions with the remaining marinade and let them sit while the fish soaks.
Grill the fish on a hot oiled grill or broiler for 4 minutes per side until charred and at least 145°F inside. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onions with the whole pepper and bay leaf for 20 minutes, stirring, until very soft and golden.
Add [[0.5 cup]] water and simmer 10 minutes more until saucy.
Nestle the grilled fish into the onions and warm through for 5 minutes. Serve over white rice.
nt: Best swap: chicken thighs are the classic alternative; a habanero stands in for scotch bonnet.
